stories.title: Complete the shared lint toolchain and safe fix command
stories.description: Reconcile the baseline from pull request #32, pin the additional shared lint dependencies required by this issue, and add a root lint:fix command that uses the same configuration as lint.
acceptanceCriteria: All lint dependencies are pinned through Yarn and no global installation is required
yarn lint and yarn lint:fix use the same versioned root ESLint configuration
yarn lint:fix applies only supported fixes and does not format, generate, or rewrite unrelated content
The baseline repository passes yarn lint after the toolchain change
stories.notes: Pull request #32 already added pinned ESLint, TypeScript ESLint, React, and React Hooks dependencies plus yarn lint. The missing lint:fix command and final plugin set require current implementation and verification.

stories.title: Enforce type-aware TypeScript correctness by environment
stories.description: Enable type-aware TypeScript linting and targeted browser, Node.js, test, Storybook, configuration, package, and game overrides without treating every TypeScript file as browser code.
acceptanceCriteria: Type-aware promise, unused-code, correctness, and unsafe TypeScript rules run against the intended TypeScript projects
Browser, React, Node.js, test, Storybook, generator, configuration, package, and game files receive only appropriate globals and rules
Unsafe any usage, floating or misused promises, and unused code fail with actionable file and line diagnostics
The configuration remains one shared root flat configuration with targeted overrides
stories.notes: The current config uses non-type-aware TypeScript recommended rules and assigns browser globals to every TS/TSX file. Current evidence does not satisfy typed unsafe or promise enforcement and precise environment separation.

stories.title: Enforce React, hooks, accessibility, and import correctness
stories.description: Complete React linting with hooks, accessibility, and import correctness rules appropriate to the host, Storybook, and game-facing React source.
acceptanceCriteria: React and React Hooks correctness rules remain enforced for JSX and TSX
Representative accessibility violations fail lint with actionable diagnostics
Representative invalid, unresolved, duplicate, or disordered imports fail according to the documented import policy
Rules that conflict with the React JSX runtime, TypeScript, Storybook, or generated boundaries are resolved through narrow documented overrides
stories.notes: Pull request #32 enabled React recommended, JSX runtime, and React Hooks flat recommended rules. Accessibility and dedicated import enforcement are not installed or demonstrated.

stories.title: Guarantee automatic workspace coverage and deliberate exclusions
stories.description: Make repository discovery automatically cover current and future game and package workspaces while narrowly excluding generated, imported, dependency, coverage, and build output.
acceptanceCriteria: Host source, shared packages, every game workspace, Storybook, tests, scripts, generators, and handwritten wrappers are linted
A representative newly created game or package workspace cannot silently bypass yarn lint
Generated Mamba snapshots, imported Mamba sources, dependencies, coverage, and build outputs are excluded without excluding generators or handwritten wrappers
The exclusion list is narrow, versioned, and verified against unexpected lint:fix modifications
stories.notes: The current eslint dot-glob covers existing authored JS/TS files and excludes Mamba snapshots and standard outputs, but no current proof establishes future workspace coverage or safe fix boundaries.

stories.title: Require narrow suppressions with durable reasons
stories.description: Strengthen suppression policy so every exceptional inline directive is narrowly scoped, has a specific durable reason, and is represented exactly once in the reviewed allowlist.
acceptanceCriteria: Unapproved, broad, duplicate, stale, or reasonless ESLint suppressions fail repository policy
Approved suppressions identify the exact file, line, directive, affected rule, and specific rationale
Repository guidance requires the narrowest practical directive and explains the review path
Representative accepted and rejected suppression cases are automated
stories.notes: Pull request #32 added exact file/line/directive allowlisting and a minimum-length external rationale. Current evidence does not prove inline reasons, affected-rule specificity, broad-directive rejection, or representative policy cases.

stories.title: Prove representative lint failures and safe fixes
stories.description: Add isolated deterministic proofs for the rule families, environment overrides, workspace discovery, exclusions, suppression policy, warning behavior, and lint:fix safety.
acceptanceCriteria: Representative TypeScript, React, hooks, accessibility, import, promise, unused, unsafe, and environment violations return nonzero for the intended reason
Warnings fail the canonical lint command
Representative supported fixes are applied by yarn lint:fix and then pass yarn lint
Generated, imported, and unrelated files remain unchanged during fix proofs
Proofs reject unrelated setup failures as successful evidence
stories.notes: The existing fail-closed harness proves one JavaScript no-unused-vars lint failure. It does not yet cover the issue's remaining rule families, workspace bypass, exclusions, warnings, or fix safety.

stories.title: Reconcile local, workflow, and merge-gate integration
stories.description: Keep the canonical local command, continuous integration workflow, workflow policy, Ralph completion contract, and protected merge gate aligned with the completed lint implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: Every pull request and main update runs the same yarn lint command and pinned dependencies used locally
Lint output is retained with actionable file and line diagnostics and zero allowed warnings
Workflow policy rejects removal or weakening of lint and its representative proofs
A representative lint failure prevents the required protected check from succeeding
Ralph and future agentic workflows use the same lint completion contract
stories.notes: Pull request #32 integrated yarn lint into the required composite Continuous integration check and policy guard. Re-verify live protected-check behavior and update the contract only after the completed issue #27 rules and proofs exist.

stories.title: Document decisions and reconcile every acceptance criterion
stories.description: Document local usage, formatting separation, plugin and rule choices, environment overrides, workspace discovery, exclusions, suppression reasons, fix safety, continuous integration behavior, and final issue evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Documentation explains yarn lint and yarn lint:fix, including their boundary from Prettier formatting
Rule families, environment overrides, automatic workspace coverage, exclusions, and suppression approval are documented
The final evidence explicitly distinguishes what pull request #32 delivered from what issue #27 added
Every issue acceptance criterion maps to current passing local or continuous integration evidence
All repository-required validation commands pass
stories.notes: Existing continuous integration documentation describes the baseline lint command and suppression allowlist but not the complete issue #27 design or lint:fix behavior.
